sources.outlet: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society (Ryskina et al.), abstract via Europe PMC
sources.quote: There was a small statistically significant decrease in 5-star ratings after a change in ownership (-0.09 points on a 5-point scale
sources.searcher_note: National study of ownership changes 2016-2022. Also finds homes already rated 1-star were more likely to change owners. Window ends before most of the lead's 2022-2024 cohort; before/after design, not a same-state peer gap. PubMed and PMC pages are behind a captcha, so the Europe PMC record is used.

sources.quote: Most acquired facilities showed indications of financial struggles, including lower star ratings and occupancy, plus a higher percentage of stays covered by Medicaid
sources.searcher_note: Trade coverage of the Ryskina study: ratings fall about 0.1 star after a sale. Also carries an operator-side consultant saying ratings improve over time after the sale (partial disagreement).

sources.quote: Overall quality ratings decreased slightly with ownership change, by about 0.1 points on the 5-star scale.
sources.searcher_note: University write-up of the same study, 2016-2022 ownership changes.

sources.outlet: HHS Office of the Assistant Secretary for Planning and Evaluation (ASPE)
sources.quote: The ASPE analyses also found that SNFs with overall lower star quality ratings experience a change of ownership more often than SNFs with higher quality ratings.
sources.searcher_note: HHS research brief on skilled nursing ownership changes 2016-2021: lower-rated homes change hands more often. Dated June 2024, no day given. Pattern only.

sources.quote: By early 2026, star ratings for five of the nursing homes declined, with two of them dropping from five to two stars.
sources.searcher_note: Commentary piece: 10 Rhode Island homes bought by two private equity firms (Tryko, Kadima) in 2022; 5 declined in stars by early 2026. A state example inside the lead's sale window, not the national cohort.

notes: Only pattern coverage found. Nothing names this cohort: for-profit homes with an operating company formed 2022 to Sept 2024. No source has the 944 homes, the 0.28-star gap vs same-state for-profit peers, or the 52% one- or two-star share. Closest is Ryskina et al. (JAGS 2024, 2016-2022): a -0.09 star before/after drop, and homes already rated 1-star were more likely to be sold. That selection point fits the lead's caveat that 'worse after the change' didn't survive matching. ASPE (June 2024, 2016-2021) says lower-rated homes change owners more often. Private-equity coverage (the AARP report via McKnight's, 3.4 to 2.9 stars) wasn't fetchable (HTTP 402), so it's not recorded. Health Affairs 2016, 'Low-Quality Nursing Homes Were More Likely Than Other Nursing Homes To Be Bought Or Sold By Chains In 1993-2010', returned 403. A Skilled Nursing News piece from July 2026 on the star-rating changes has nothing on sales. No July-Sept 2026 coverage of the pattern found.
